# SPD-018 — Spud's Stop hook: children that never returned, and only its own session's members

## Brief
hook_stop lists only members with a final stop and no outcome, so a planned row that was never spawned, or a child still running when Spud finished its parent, is invisible to Spud's Law 9 block while it holds a fan-out and a concurrency slot for ever. SPD-015 closed exactly that blind spot one level down (alive_children in hook_subagent_stop holds a lead for a child still alive); the ticket told me to leave hook_stop as is, so Spud's own turn still ends with those rows unseen.

Evidence: The exploration probe of 2026-09-12 (probes/lead-hold-20260912T201448 in my session scratchpad): the child ran 35 s past its lead and the -p session ended with it active, Result recorded, no outcome, never named by Spud's Stop. In bin/spud, hook_stop requires m.stopped_at IS NOT NULL; alive_children() in the same file is the query that would cover the rest, with the same once-only shape.

Added by Spud on 2026-09-13: hook_stop is not scoped to a session either. Eric now runs tickets in parallel sessions (SPD-024 in one, SPD-012 in another), and the query takes every member ledger-wide with a final stop and no outcome, so a member returned in one session holds every other session's Stop once with a Law 9 block naming a member that session never spawned, and invites it to record a verdict on work it never saw. Scope the block to the members the stopping session spawned (spawn_requests.session_id, which PreToolUse(Agent) already records, or the session bound to the member), and show another session's unrecorded members, if at all, as context rather than a block. Evidence: bin/spud hook_stop, whose SELECT has no session condition; spawn_requests.session_id, already used by hook_subagent_stop's oldest-unbound binding.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, the persona tier, no children. Enforcement hooks took fable in [[SPD-008]]; Eric ruled Fable out again (2026-09-13), so opus, with Spud reading the diff and rerunning the suite at return. At most two headless probes, on haiku, in scratch roots, and only for what the hooks docs leave open: whether a subagent's hook payloads carry the main session's `session_id`, and whether a Bash command can see its session id. Design decided at start: Spud's Stop hook blocks a session only for members that session spawned (a member with no recorded session still blocks every session, as today); it adds planned rows that were never spawned and children still running under a finished parent, each held once; a member of another session is never blocked on, and `board --brief`, which SessionStart injects, marks a returned member not yet recorded so a later or parallel session sees it. [[SPD-012]] runs in another session on its own branch and also changes `bin/spud`, so the two merges may touch the same file; Eric merges each when he says.
